Ivy Tran: hi all  I'm about to open my first PR touching api/clients and a small docs update. quick run-down: branch naming, commit conventions, who to request for review, and any small PR etiquette?

Marcus Hale: welcome Ivy! quick rules we follow: branch from main; name pattern: <team>-<ticket>-short (e.g., runtime-456-add-retries). commit header: `area(scope): brief summary` (<=50 chars). include a test plan and screenshot if UI.

Priya Shah: For cross-package changes add a short description of what packages changed and run `make quick-test` to run only impacted unit tests. If you change public client interfaces, add a changelog entry under `docs/changes/`.

Marcus Hale: reviewers: pick 1 owner from CODEOWNERS (auto-requested) and 1 peer. if it's infra-ish tag @eng-infra. For runtime/client changes tag @eng-platform. We usually ask for at least one approving review before merge.

Ivy Tran: how strict are we on commit granularity? can I squash when merging?

Priya Shah: prefer small logical commits during development. final policy: squash-and-merge for single logical change. keep separate commits for independent refactors. we do preserve commit messages by putting a good PR description.

CI-bot: CI pipeline summary: pre-commit, ruff/black, pytest unit, mypy, license check, and a quick integration test if `api/` changed. Full e2e runs only on staging pipeline. Logs will be posted to the PR.

Marcus Hale: PR etiquette: short description, link to ticket, add `changes:` if user-visible, add labels (area/api, breaking-change if applicable). If you need an expedited review, add a short note and `@eng-oncall` if it's a release blocker.

Ivy Tran: thanks! last thing: any local commands to speed up iteration?

Priya Shah: use `make dev-venv` then `invoke test.unit --filter api` or `pytest -k "test_client*" -q`. run `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --all-files` to skip slow hooks while still checking. See CONTRIBUTING.md for more tips.

onboard-bot: Tip: newcomers often forget to sign-off. run `git commit -s` or `--signoff` if contributions require DCO. Also check PR checklist before requesting review: https://redwood.example/docs/pr-checklist :robot_face:

Ivy Tran: great, I'll follow this and ping when it's up. really appreciate the guidance! :thumbsup:
